sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Track 3, Lesson 3.2 of Dataset Fundamentals: Core Ethical Principles. Global consensus across the OECD AI Principles, the IEEE Global Initiative, the Belmont Report, and the Montreal Declaration converges on five foundational pillars: Non-Maleficence, Fairness, Transparency, Accountability, and Respect for Autonomy.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: In software engineering, ethical values are too often dismissed as decorative slogans. Today we transform each pillar into deterministic CI/CD verification tests, Rawlsian distributive justice bounds, formal fairness metrics, and actionable adverse action explanations.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let us examine Table 3.1: The Operationalization Matrix. First, Non-Maleficence asks whether a dataset poses foreseeable physical, financial, or psychological harm, bounded by subgroup worst-case risk sup R sub g less than or equal to tau max. Second, Fairness tests whether errors differ across demographic classes using Disparate Impact Ratio at least 0.80 and Equalized Odds disparity.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Third, Transparency verifies decision explanations via Shapley values and adverse action ranking. Fourth, Accountability requires cryptographic provenance hashes and human escalation service-level agreements. Fifth, Respect for Autonomy demands granular opt-in toggles, Dynamic Consent registries, and deletion DAGs—explicitly banning GDPR Article 7 paragraph 4 dark patterns like pre-ticked boxes.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: When evaluating whether a dataset deployment is ethical, moral philosophy gives us two contrasting social welfare functions. Utilitarian Aggregate Welfare sums utility across all N individuals and divides by N. Because it averages across everyone, a model that benefits 90 percent of people while inflicting severe harm on a 10 percent minority still scores high.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: In contrast, John Rawls's Maximin Distributive Justice evaluates a system strictly by the expected utility of its least-advantaged subgroup g. Furthermore, to operationalize Non-Maleficence against catastrophic tail events, we compute the Benefit-to-Risk Ratio BRR as expected benefit divided by expected cost plus gamma times the standard deviation of cost, where gamma quantifies downside risk aversion.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Algorithmic fairness formalizes three competing mathematical definitions across sensitive groups G in zero and one. First, Demographic Parity requires positive prediction rates to be independent of group membership, operationalized via the EEOC Four-Fifths Rule: Disparate Impact Ratio at least 0.80.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Second, Equalized Odds—introduced by Hardt, Price, and Srebro—requires predictions Y-hat to be conditionally independent of G given the true outcome Y, bounding both False Positive Rate and True Positive Rate disparities by epsilon fair. Third, Predictive Parity enforces outcome calibration within groups: given a positive prediction, the true outcome probability must be equal across cohorts.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Proven independently by Alexandra Chouldechova and Jon Kleinberg in 2017, the Fairness Impossibility Theorem establishes a hard algebraic barrier: whenever true condition base rates differ across demographic groups, no imperfect classifier can simultaneously satisfy Equalized Odds and Predictive Parity.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: By Bayes' Theorem, Positive Predictive Value equals 1 divided by 1 plus the odds ratio 1 minus p over p times FPR over TPR. If FPR over TPR stays constant under Equalized Odds while base prevalence p differs, calibration must diverge! Meanwhile, to operationalize Transparency, Lundberg and Lee's Shapley value phi j averages marginal feature contributions across all subsets S, providing unique axiomatic explanations.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let us simulate Obermeyer's landmark 2019 healthcare audit across 1,000 synthetic patient encounters: 800 majority Group A patients and 200 minority Group B patients.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Start with Preset 1, Biased Cost Proxy, and observe why Utilitarian Social Welfare appears solid at 0.88 even while the Rawlsian Maximin floor collapses and minority clinical recall plunges! Then switch to Preset 3, Biomarker Grounding, to restore Equalized Odds and EEOC Disparate Impact parity.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Time for Active Recall Checkpoint 1! An ICU deploys a sepsis onset predictor where true sepsis prevalence is 12 percent among elderly patients aged 65 and older, versus 3 percent among young adults under 30. Hospital leadership demands simultaneous Equalized Odds and Predictive Parity across both cohorts.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Use Bayes' Theorem and Chouldechova's Impossibility Theorem to diagnose why this specification cannot be satisfied by an imperfect classifier. Select Option A, B, or C below.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: In a landmark Science audit covering algorithms affecting over 200 million US patients, Obermeyer and colleagues uncovered how an innocuous proxy label inflicted massive racial harm. Designers wanted to triage high-need patients into nurse care management, so they substituted total annual healthcare expenditure as a proxy for biological illness severity.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Because systemic access and insurance barriers caused health systems to spend far less on Black patients than white patients with identical chronic disease burdens, Black patients had to be drastically sicker to reach the same dollar risk score. Replacing expenditure with active biomarkers like HbA1c and chronic condition counts eliminated the gap, boosting qualified Black patient enrollment by 84 percent.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Case Study 2 illustrates historical selection contamination: in 2018, Amazon disbanded its automated AI resume ranker trained on 10 years of predominantly male engineering hires. The NLP model penalized words like 'women's' and graduates of all-women colleges—and even after deleting gender terms, reconstructed bias through latent masculine action verbs.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Case Study 3 is ProPublica's 2016 audit of COMPAS criminal recidivism scoring. COMPAS achieved Predictive Parity—around 60 percent re-arrest calibration regardless of race. Yet because base re-arrest rates differed, COMPAS severely violated Equalized Odds: Black non-reoffenders were mislabeled High Risk at 44.9 percent versus 23.5 percent for white non-reoffenders, while white re-offenders were mislabeled Low Risk nearly twice as often.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Under the US Equal Credit Opportunity Act and GDPR Article 22, whenever an automated credit underwriting model declines an applicant, lenders must issue a structured Adverse Action Notice containing concrete SHAP attribution scores—such as Delinquency History at minus 0.38 and Revolving Utilization at minus 0.24—paired with actionable recourse guidance.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Equally critical in credit underwriting is avoiding the Fairness Through Blindness fallacy. Deleting race, ethnicity, and ZIP code still produces severe disparate impact when remaining features X—such as smartphone OS, college, merchant codes, and payment timestamps—retain high mutual information I of X and G with the protected class.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Inserting a human reviewer purely as a rubber stamp does not establish GDPR Article 22 accountability. When judges approve algorithmic bail scores 98.4 percent of the time without reading defense dossiers, Automation Bias turns the human operator into a 'moral crumple zone' absorbing institutional blame.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Similarly, under GDPR Article 7 paragraph 3 Respect for Autonomy, merely running SQL DELETE when a user withdraws consent fails because neural weights retain memorized gradient updates delta theta equals minus eta times grad L. True consent revocation demands exact or approximate Machine Unlearning pipelines such as SISA—Sharded, Isolated, Sliced, and Aggregated training.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let us verify Chouldechova's Impossibility Theorem experimentally using Bayes' calibration equation right inside the studio.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Adjust base prevalence p sub 0 and p sub 1, False Positive Rate, True Positive Rate, and the Normative Priority mode below. Observe how enforcing Equalized Odds forces Positive Predictive Value calibration to diverge whenever base rates differ—and how enforcing Predictive Parity forces FPR disparity just like COMPAS.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Time for Active Recall Checkpoint 2! A fintech credit model strips race and ZIP code yet still audits a Disparate Impact Ratio of 0.58. Meanwhile, to comply with GDPR, its human reviewers rubber-stamp 98.4 percent of scores, and user consent revocations simply execute SQL DELETE.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Identify the exact engineering diagnosis explaining why all three practices fail Fairness, Accountability, and Autonomy. Select Option A, B, or C below.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: To move from failure diagnostics to robust architecture, engineering teams deploy concrete safeguards across every pillar. Instead of Fairness Through Blindness, teams apply adversarial debiasing, subgroup error-rate regularization, and counterfactual data augmentation.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Instead of rubber-stamp human approvals, teams introduce meaningful friction—requiring written rationales, double-blind peer reviews, and automated escalation thresholds. And instead of coercive EULAs or raw SQL drops, teams adopt Dynamic Informed Consent ledgers backed by SISA sharded unlearning.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let us inspect our production fairness and distributive welfare gatekeeper in ethical_welfare_audit.py. Using Pydantic V2 and vectorized NumPy masking, EthicalFairnessAuditor evaluates true positive rate, false positive rate, selection rate, and balanced utility for every protected subgroup.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Notice the strict release condition is_deployable: Rawlsian Maximin welfare must reach at least 0.70, Disparate Impact Ratio must meet the EEOC 0.80 floor, and Equalized Odds disparity must stay below 0.15. Under the biased proxy simulation, the minority cohort gets zero predictions, crashing rawlsian welfare below 0.60 and blocking CI/CD automatically.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let us summarize the five core ethical engineering takeaways from Lesson 3.2. First: Operationalize ethics into deterministic code contracts—Rawlsian maximin floors and bounded disparity checks. Second: Avoid the proxy label trap—never substitute healthcare spend or historical arrest records for true human need.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Third: Respect the Fairness Impossibility Theorem—Demographic Parity, Equalized Odds, and Predictive Parity cannot coexist when base rates differ, so document deliberate normative choices. Fourth: Favor distributive justice over aggregate utility—evaluate systems by their least-advantaged cohort. Fifth: Provide axiomatic transparency and recourse via Shapley attribution. Next in Lesson 3.3, we investigate Utility Dilemmas and Real-World Consequences!
